The proposed framework is designed to actively select the tactile readings that maximize the improvement in shape reconstruction accuracy.
The framework consists of a haptic simulator, a mesh-based reconstruction model, and data-driven policies.
The haptic simulator uses high-resolution vision-based tactile sensors.
The Chamfer distance is used as the distance metric in the active touch formulation.
50 points are uniformly placed on a sphere to define an action space.
The objective of the data-driven policies is to select the positions of the next touches to acquire in order to maximize the similarity between predicted and target shape.
Mesh embeddings of reduced dimensionality are used to facilitate the learning of the policies.
Over 25k CAD models are used in the dataset.
The proposed framework outperforms random baselines by up to 18%.
Wonik's Allegro Hand is used in the simulator.
A graph convolutional network (GCN) is used in the reconstruction model.
The first GCN is used to learn an object prior.
The second GCN is used to refine the object belief through a 2-step deformation process.
The Chamfer distance is used as the type of distance metric in the reconstruction model.
The proposed framework is designed to handle a variable number of touch charts.
The proposed framework is designed to handle a variable number of vision charts.
The proposed framework is designed to handle a variable number of touch signals.
The proposed framework is designed to handle a variable number of vision signals.
The proposed framework is designed to produce a surface prediction in a single model pass.
The proposed framework is designed to be fully data-driven.
The proposed framework is designed to use learned object priors.
The proposed framework is designed to use learned exploration strategies.
The proposed framework is designed to be trained and evaluated on a large-scale dataset.
The proposed framework is designed to be publicly available on GitHub.
